newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - Gilts to steal a march on Europe.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - Gilts to steal a march on Europe.

text.p: British gilts will lure investors away from core European bonds over the coming months, and are expected to improve their outperformance of Bunds by the end of the year, analysts said on Tuesday.

With the Bank of England's interest rate policy on hold for now after four rate rises in as many months, British interest rates may be reaching their upper limit, while Europe has yet to embark on a tightening cycle, they said.
"There is going to be a prolonged period when UK interest rates are unchanged," said Eric Fishwick at Nikko Europe.

"But in Europe they are ahead of what must be a relatively prolonged cyclical interest rate tightening. You are going to see less favourable short rate trends in Europe than in either the U.S. or the UK," international economist Fishwick said in London.

He said German interest rates were low in both nominal and real terms and with the German economy picking up, market expectations were for the Bundesbank to tighten rates aggressively by the year end.
"You could certainly look for the spread to be back below 100 quite comfortably, something like 75 to 80 basis points by the end of the year," he said.
At 1103 GMT, the 10-year gilt/Bund spread was at 151 basis points compared with 185 in early January.
Huw Roberts, European bond strategist at NatWest Markets saw a less dramatic spread narrowing to 120 basis points by the year end.
"There is a bear market coming because of the (expected) German rate hike and factors in the U.S., but gilts will probably be able to narrow the spreads to core Europe," he said.
John McNeill, bond strategist at I.D.E.A. also said Britain was close to the top of the tightening cycle.

"In terms of what is priced into the market, gilts have got the potential for quite a bit of good news over the next month whereas some of the other European markets are going to need good news just to stand still," he said.
However in the short-term it is not all plain sailing for Britain.
The reduction in gilts supply suggested by strong public sector debt repayment data on Monday may not be enough to outweigh any strength in consumer spending seen in Wednesday's retail sales figures.
"This data is good for gilts but it comes with a bit of a health warning attached," said Roberts.
The data showed a public debt repayment of 3.875 billion stg in July with most of the improvement coming from the increase in value-added tax (VAT) receipts.

It was not clear how much of this was due to manufacturing and how much was due to consumption. But seen alongside other economic data the inference was that it was from the consumer sector and would therefore suggest strong retail sales figures, Roberts said.

"If that is true then it isn't necessarily such great news," he said. "Now the BoE has declared itself to be on hold (on rates), it leaves gilts very much at the mercy of each individual economic report."
A Reuters consensus of analysts forecast July retail sales to rise 0.3 pct on the month, compared with 0.6 pct rise in June. Year-on-year expectations were for a 5.8 pct rise.
In particular, Roberts said the front end could be vulnerable as strong data would suggest the pause in rates was only temporary.
Fishwick agreed. He said there was a long-term downside risk from the data rather than any alteration to immediate prospects at the next monetary meeting.
